title: Zero-Downtime Table Bloat Remediation: pg_repack vs VACUUM FULL
realWorldScenario: Due to a buggy batch job that updated 5 million rows 20 times in a loop, the `inventory` table ballooned from 4 GB to 85 GB. Queries doing sequential scans are now 20x slower. Running `VACUUM FULL inventory;` is rejected by leadership because it requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for 3 hours.
questionStatement: Explain why standard `VACUUM` cannot return space to the OS. Compare `VACUUM FULL` with `pg_repack`. Detail step-by-step how `pg_repack` rebuilds the table and all indexes online without holding exclusive locks, and explain its log-replay catch-up phase.
expectedConcepts: Why standard VACUUM only updates FSM and cannot return middle pages to OS
VACUUM FULL ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock blocking all reads and writes
pg_repack shadow table, trigger logging, and online bulk copy
Brief catalog pointer swap (relfilenode) for zero downtime
hints: Why can standard VACUUM only truncate pages from the end of the file?
How does pg_repack capture concurrent writes that happen while it copies rows?
How does it finalize the replacement in catalog tables?
